_readme: Provenance for every file in photos/. One entry per image.
THE RECORD, ESTABLISHED BY OSCAR 2026-08-09: he took every photograph in this
directory himself. They are his own work and his to use, commercially included.
This file previously said the opposite — 146 photos marked "unrecorded /
licence unknown" on the assumption they had been fetched from Wikimedia by
plant-images-tool.js. That inference was wrong on the facts:
- the tool has never been run against the live API (README says so, and it
needs network access the build container did not have);
- plant-images/ was never committed, because nothing was ever downloaded;
- CARD-PROTOCOL.md photo register describes ~100 of these images in detail
and never once records an external source — they are "real photo",
"real garden shot", or cutouts and composites made from Oscars own shots.
EXIF cannot corroborate either way: add-plant.js re-encodes every photo through
a canvas, which strips all metadata.
source    : "oscar" (his own photograph) or "oscar-ai" (he generated it with an
AI tool rather than a camera). "wikimedia" exists for anything
plant-images-tool.js fetches in future; nothing carries it today.
licence   : what is actually known. NEVER guess one.
commit    : the commit that added the file, recovered from git history.
The two AI images are the only open question, and it is a real one: output
rights for AI-generated images depend on the generators terms, so they are
marked commercialUseCleared:false until someone checks. Every photograph is
cleared.

photos.note: Samsung Galaxy S24 capture, AI-edited on device. The source PNG carried a C2PA manifest: c2pa.edited, softwareAgent 'Photo assist', digitalSourceType compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia, plus an 'AI-generated content' watermark burned into the pixels (it lands under the aspect band on the card). Staging re-encodes through a canvas, which strips the manifest, so this entry is the only surviving record. Same class as the Primula vialii held on 2026-08-09 — dealt rather than held because the card is a one-off gift, not stock imagery.
